recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. If FHIR-I wants validators to emit warnings whenever a canonical resource has version but no versionAlgorithm[x], open or apply an explicit follow-up decision scoped to that broad validation impact; otherwise no FHIR-core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-26370.
issue_request: FHIR-26370 was Published with a Persuasive with Modification resolution asking for a technical mechanism to retrieve the most recent canonical resource version: CanonicalResource.versionAlgorithm[x] as Coding|string, an extensible VersionAlgorithm binding with initial comparison codes, FHIRPath comparison comments, and warning guidance when a canonical version is present without a declared algorithm.
initial_application: Commit f5a3f369a4dc96aa0f75a2c75f90a258388a9a5a explicitly applied FHIR-26370 by adding CanonicalResource.versionAlgorithm[x] and the version-algorithm CodeSystem/ValueSet. Later commits, including c01ed3edbe8a92201a72a348a4daf757fc8c2526 and other canonical-alignment work, propagated versionAlgorithm[x] to concrete canonical resources such as ValueSet, while FHIR-35834 commits added and clarified the $current-canonical operation that uses versionAlgorithm to compare canonical versions.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini keeps CanonicalResource, ValueSet, CodeSystem, and OperationDefinition in current build scope. Later decisions reinforce the current model: FHIR-27920 centralized canonical versioning guidance, FHIR-39268 kept versionAlgorithm[x] on individual canonical resources as the best available compromise, FHIR-38159 aligned terminology resources with the CanonicalResource change, and FHIR-40523 confirmed the extensible binding strength. Current source/references.html says canonical resources SHOULD declare versionAlgorithm[x] because determining current versions is problematic without it, while $current-canonical allows servers to infer, default, or reject ambiguous algorithms when the element is absent or inconsistent.
reconciliation: No source files were changed. The current source contains the requested versionAlgorithm[x] element, comparison terminology, ValueSet participation, most-current retrieval operation, and central missing-algorithm guidance. A literal validator warning invariant for missing versionAlgorithm[x] is not present, but adding one now would broadly change validation and QA behavior across canonical resources; the current SHOULD-level guidance preserves the implementer-facing rule without needing a new source edit in this reconciliation.
